claims.text: Multiphase refractory high-entropy alloys with BCC/B2 microstructures may exhibit a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during isothermal aging at 600–800 °C.
The proposed non-monotonic ductility transition is driven by evolution of B2 chemical ordering and redistribution of BCC and B2 phase fractions.
A relevant initial microstructure can consist of a disordered BCC matrix containing fine-scale ordered B2 regions or precipitates.
A relevant initial microstructure can alternatively be superalloy-like, with cuboidal BCC pockets in a continuous ordered B2 matrix.
NbMoTaW-based alloys are an example of the proposed multiphase BCC/B2 material class.
The relevant aging window is 600–800 °C for 10–100 hours.
Water quenching preserves the aged high-temperature phase fractions.
Aging progressively increases the long-range order parameter of the B2 phase.
Long-term aging can increase the B2 phase fraction at the expense of the BCC phase fraction.
Aging-induced phase redistribution can move the ductile BCC phase through a connectivity or percolation threshold.
An ordered B2 matrix provides high strength but poor ductility.
B2 ordering reduces ductility by restricting dislocation mobility in the ordered phase.
Further aging can produce coarser, discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous disordered BCC matrix.
Formation or restoration of a continuous BCC matrix during further aging can recover ductility.
Additional slip systems may become active in the ordered phase during prolonged aging and contribute to ductility recovery.
Tensile elongation will decrease after approximately 20–50 hours and increase again after more than 80 hours of aging.
The as-processed BCC/B2 RHEA has greater than 20% elongation because of its fine, disordered or partially ordered dual-phase microstructure.
The non-monotonic transition is limited to alloys having a BCC/B2 dual-phase constitution.
The VEC boundary for the proposed transition in dual-phase alloys is not established.
Secondary phases such as sigma phase may cause embrittlement after very long aging times.

contradictions.description: The initial state permits a continuous ordered B2 matrix, which the mechanism associates with poor ductility, while the baseline broadly assigns the as-processed condition greater than 20% elongation.
The stated aging duration is limited to 10–100 hours, but the proposed falsification series includes a 120-hour condition.
